why.text: Flat alluvial plains beside the Tagus, clay-limestone hills and sandy heath soils, under a moderate climate with about 2,800 hours of sun a year.

styles.text: Red, white and rosé wines, plus quality sparkling wine and fortified (licoroso) wine.

climate.text: Moderate climate; mean temperatures 15.5 to 16.5 °C, about 2,800 sun hours a year and 750 mm of rain a year. It is a little wetter around Tomar in the north and drier around Coruche in the south.

soil.text: Three zones: the Campo has fertile alluvial soils beside the Tagus, mostly limy. The Bairro has clay-limestone soils in gentle hills. The Charneca, south of the river, has sandy, moderately fertile soils.

altitude.text: Cartaxo's Campo is flat at 6 to 10 m; its Bairro hills reach 200 m in places.

tastes.text: Whites run pale lemon to gold, reds ruby to deep red turning garnet and brownish, rosés pink to salmon. All show young fruity and/or floral aromas, gaining more complex tertiary aromas with age.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional term; wines with a quality term must score at least 65.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Traditional term; quality-term wines need outstanding structure and balance.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Quality sparkling wine, at least 10.5% alcohol; bottle fermentation, or tank with nine months' ageing.

styles.name: Vinho licoroso
styles.text: Fortified wine; neutral wine spirit may be added to fermenting must; at least 17.5%.
